en.title: Josh Hartnett’s ‘Below’ and Ben Affleck’s ‘Animals’ Conquer Netflix Charts
en.summary: Josh Hartnett's new horror series 'Below' has landed at the top of Netflix's English TV charts, while Ben Affleck's thriller 'Animals' also made a strong debut. This week's Top 10 reveals a fascinating mix of original content and licensed powerhouses.
en.body:
The streaming wars continue to heat up, and this week, Netflix's Top 10 charts for October 5th to October 11th, 2026, reveal some clear winners. Leading the charge on the English TV side is **Josh Hartnett**'s new limited series, **‘Below’**, which has officially landed at the number one spot. The horror-thriller, which has been a bright spot for the genre on the platform, garnered an impressive 17 million views. Meanwhile, **Ben Affleck**’s new thriller, **‘Animals’**, has also made a significant splash, debuting at the top of the English Movies chart. The film's performance comes amidst some pre-release buzz related to Affleck's involvement with an AI company he sold to Netflix, a narrative that has certainly added a layer of complexity to its reception.

Beyond these high-profile debuts, the charts also showcase the enduring power of licensed content. The *Ice Age* movies, recently added as part of a new Disney licensing deal, have completely dominated the movie side, occupying half of the available spots on the English-language list. This dominance underscores how familiar, beloved franchises can still command massive viewership, even in an era of abundant original content. It will be interesting to see how long these animated favorites can maintain their grip on the charts.

## A Mixed Bag of Fan Reception

While **‘Below’** is a chart-topper, its critical reception appears to be more divisive. Online discussions reveal a spectrum of opinions, with some viewers praising its tight, mystery-driven narrative in a confined setting, while others are less impressed. One particularly blunt review on IMDb stated, "Everything about this show sucks. I'm giving it a 2/10 only because the ending of episode 5 was the only good thing about the entire show." Another viewer questioned the show's logic, citing an implausible scene involving a boat moving a massive block of ice, and critiquing the acting. This mixed feedback suggests that while **‘Below’** has captured a significant audience, its narrative and execution may not resonate universally, despite its number one ranking.

## What's Next for Netflix's Top Performers

This week's chart performance for **‘Below’** and **‘Animals’** certainly sets a strong precedent for their future on the platform. While renewal details for limited series like **‘Below’** are typically not announced, its strong viewership numbers could influence future genre projects. For **‘Animals’**, its debut success will likely be closely monitored by Netflix executives as they assess the performance of high-profile star vehicles. Meanwhile, the continued dominance of licensed content like the *Ice Age* franchise highlights ongoing strategic decisions regarding content acquisition.

content_raw: Picture Credits: Netflix Welcome to your weekly breakdown of the biggest hits and misses on Netflix. Every Tuesday, Netflix updates its global viewing metrics, and today we’re diving into the Top 10 charts for the week of October 5th to October 11th, 2026. This week’s data gives us a fascinating mixed bag to analyze. We’re tracking a highly scrutinized blockbuster debut from Ben Affleck, a new Josh Hartnett horror-thriller series proving to be a bright spot for the genre, and an impressive, gravity-defying second-week surge for East of Eden . Plus, we’re seeing the sheer, undeniable power of licensed content completely taking over the movie side. As we’ve tracked all week, the Ice Age movies, arriving as part of a new Disney licensing deal, have topped the charts worldwide and took up half of the available spots on the English-language list this week. Not bad at all; we’ll see how many stay next week.  A few big omissions this week from the Top 10s: Haunted Hotel , which returned for Season 2, didn’t get into the English TV Top 10s, nor did the second season of Is It Cake? Halloween . Netflix Poland’s Less of a Stranger was missing from the non-English movie list, with Real Mean (Season 2) also skipping the TV side. Leading a number of comedy documentaries, Who Is Martin Mull? is also absent from the movie chart. Animals Debuts at #1 on English Movies  Ben Affleck’s new movie Animals has been released with a bit of a cloud over it, it must be said. Due to Affleck’s involvement with an AI company, which he sold to Netflix, many headlines and Twitter posts from handy aggregators who strip context like there’s no tomorrow have led to people coming in with preconceived notions about this particular title. It also didn’t help that most reviews, some often tainted by AI use, were on the whole mixed to bad.  Nevertheless, the movie did top the Netflix charts with 23.8M views. That’s a respectable start, though it doesn’t quite match the heights of Affleck’s early 2026 movie, The Rip , which hit 41.6M in its opening weekend, but it lands between The Whisper Man and Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man .
